prompt:
A minimalist preparation card illustration for an herbal tincture. Flat-lay top-down view of an herbal apothecary workspace on a bone #F7EFE2 surface. Composed elements: one small amber-brown glass dropper bottle with a black rubber bulb dropper, sitting upright slightly off-center upper-left; one short wide-mouth mason jar half-full of a warm amber alcohol infusion with a few herb leaves visibly suspended inside, sitting to the right; three or four fresh herb sprigs (small green leaves, simple botanical silhouettes — could be sage or thyme) scattered loosely between them; one small wooden spoon with a stubby handle resting at an angle; one tiny pile of finely chopped dried herb on the surface. The composition breathes — at least 40 percent of the image is clean empty bone-colored surface. No utensils beyond the spoon, no saucers, no text, no labels on the bottle or jar.

RENDERING STYLE: Clean modern illustration — flat base colors with smooth soft-shaded gradients. Bottle, jar, and herbs have clean confident silhouettes, not painterly brushstrokes. NO watercolor bleeds, NO paper grain, NO sketchy lines. Glass surfaces show a subtle highlight ring (single soft light pass) but no caustics or refraction effects. Warm diffuse afternoon light from upper left casts soft shadows below each object. Palette: amber, sage, warm wood, bone. Feels patient, craft-oriented, thoughtful. Recipe-card thumbnail — composition must read at small sizes. Match rendering style of tea-card-chamomile.
